options: The column must always have a value — no row can be inserted without one
The column's values must all be unique
The column must be numeric
The column can only be updated once
questions.explain: NOT NULL is the simplest constraint — it just requires a value to be present.

questions.q: What can a CHECK constraint validate that NOT NULL cannot?
options: Any boolean expression on the value, such as a range, a list of allowed values, or a pattern
Whether the value is unique across the table
Whether the value matches a value in another table
Whether the table has an index
questions.explain: CHECK goes beyond presence — it validates the value actually satisfies a condition you write.

questions.q: In AdventureWorks2012's Production.Product, what does CK_Product_ListPrice enforce?
options: ListPrice must be greater than or equal to 0.00
ListPrice must always be NULL
ListPrice must match the StandardCost exactly
ListPrice can only be set once
questions.explain: This CHECK constraint prevents a negative list price from ever being stored, regardless of what inserted it.

questions.q: Why is enforcing a validation rule with a CHECK constraint more reliable than relying on application code?
options: It's physically impossible to bypass, no matter which application, script, or person performs the INSERT/UPDATE
CHECK constraints run faster than any application code
Application code cannot perform validation at all
CHECK constraints only apply to SELECT statements
questions.explain: If even one code path forgets to validate, application-level checks can be silently bypassed; a database CHECK constraint cannot.

questions.q: What is the naming convention AdventureWorks2012 uses for CHECK constraints?
options: CK_ prefix
PK_ prefix
FK_ prefix
AK_ prefix
questions.explain: CK_ is used for CHECK constraints, distinct from PK_ (primary key), FK_ (foreign key), and AK_ (alternate/unique key).
